item.aggregated_output:
Strategy memo arithmetic verified
7:Compared with the CEO's opening **$862,000** goal, the present provisional figure is **$445,100 lower**: $862,000 − $416,900 = $445,100. That difference consists of the unsupported $410,000 projected lost-profit/tort item, $32,000 in estimated fees for Rosa and Tay that Marcus expressly waived, and approximately $3,100 in June billing error. These are corrections to the claim, not concessions extracted by Pinecrest. The February 11 email must be disclosed accurately: it waived Rosa and Tay only, but the later texts and call may support waiver or estoppel arguments as to Priya, Luis, and Keisha. [Account stated and waiver](../../library/columbia_account_stated_waiver.md).
18:Pinecrest has offered to pay the four invoices only when the conversion-fee dispute resolves. Section 2 calls for payment within 30 days and contains no such condition. We should insist on payment of $265,200 now and keep the fee dispute separate. The absence of recorded objections to those invoices supports an account-stated argument, but the invoice receipt dates and payment history remain unknown. [Account stated and waiver](../../library/columbia_account_stated_waiver.md). Pinecrest says its July 9 objection to J-4533 was timely. We cannot verify timeliness without a receipt date; the admitted double entry must be credited regardless. We should seek the full audit and time records, including any additional contested shifts.
20:Marcus says he never waived fees for the five later hires. His written February waiver was expressly limited to Rosa and Tay, which supports him. Still, his April “we'll talk” and May “call me” texts, followed by a six-minute call whose contents are unknown, could affect Priya, Luis, and Keisha. Anne and Victor have no comparable documented acquiescence. The contract provides 25% of **each person's actual first-year annualized compensation**, not 25% of an assumed common salary. Until those figures and individual introductions are proved, the $80,000 remains illustrative. [Account stated and waiver](../../library/columbia_account_stated_waiver.md).
24:We should **not** pursue the $410,000 interference/lost-profit theory to frighten Pinecrest. Pinecrest cannot tortiously interfere with its own Juniper contract. An at-will worker theory requires improper means, for which the current file supplies no evidence; consent and legitimate business purpose are further defenses. The agreement also excludes consequential damages, which is how the projected account-profit loss appears here. A complaint pressing this theory would risk dismissal, and using it as a threat without a non-frivolous basis would be improper. [Tortious interference](../../library/columbia_tortious_interference.md); [Rule 12(b)(6)](../../library/frcp_12b6.md); [Fee shifting and candor](../../library/fee_shifting_and_candor.md). Seven hires remain central to the **contract** analysis, but two fees were expressly waived.
26:The signed agreement incorporates Exhibit C. It sends disputes arising from the agreement, including arbitrability, exclusively to AAA arbitration before one arbitrator in Capital City. Neither the fact that Juniper did not read the exhibit nor its origin as a template supplies a documented ground to disregard it. The under-$25,000 small-claims exception fits none of these invoices. A Superior Court damages suit would likely be stayed or sent to arbitration, and a successful motion to compel could make Juniper liable for Pinecrest's reasonable fees and costs. The prevailing party in arbitration may also recover reasonable fees and costs; the clause works both ways. Dollar exposure cannot be reliably estimated from the present file. [FAA §§2–4](../../library/faa_2_4.md); [Fee shifting and candor](../../library/fee_shifting_and_candor.md).
35:The client has stated there is no further information about invoice delivery or payment, exact June shift credits and audit findings, the five hires' compensation/introduction dates, the May call beyond Marcus's denial of a further waiver, or a later termination notice. Those remain material unknowns. Our demand and any arbitration filing must identify estimates as estimates and correct earlier overstatements. The same is true of the prior demand Pinecrest describes but we have not seen. [Fee shifting and candor](../../library/fee_shifting_and_candor.md).
COMPLETE WITH OPEN ITEMS

Session 4 strategy memo is complete. Session 1–3 deliverables are also complete. The September 29 opposing letter describes a prior demand absent from the client file and predates the October 22 Session 1 draft; its origin and exact text remain unknown. The client has no further information on invoice receipt dates, payments or credits, exact June credit and audit, individual hire dates/introduction/compensation, or the May call beyond Bell's denial of a further fee agreement. The approximately $416,900 amount is provisional. No reliable dollar estimate of prevailing-party fee exposure is available. Session 5 awaits its settlement instruction and any new documents.

The [Session 4 strategy memo](/work/workspace/deliverable/session4/strategy_memo.md) is complete. It states that Juniper’s position has **worsened modestly** from the original Session 1 assessment: the admitted June billing error reduces the provisional contract figure from $420,000 to about **$416,900**, while Pinecrest’s response confirms a collection fight. The risks were largely visible in Session 1; the corrected draft already reflects the lower amount.

The memo recommends pressing for the **$265,200** Pinecrest has not disputed, resolving the June audit and five possible conversion fees, and using AAA arbitration if negotiation fails. Its arithmetic was checked. Remaining unknowns are recorded in [STATUS.md](/work/workspace/deliverable/STATUS.md).
